[b][color=white]U.S. 30-year yields drop to fresh record low below 2%[/color][/b][/size][/font]
[align=justify]With worries about the global economy slowing down and trade tensions around the globe increasing, the U.S bonds market reported an inversion of the yield curve, which could be an indicator of a coming recession. Even with these worries in mind, and with 30-year yields falling below short term yields, the market is confident that this is not something to be concerned about especially seeing that there is an increase in U.S consumer spending. U.S retail sales were up 0.7% in July 2019, far surpassing the 0.3% predicted rate. The day after the inversion happened and long-term yields fell below 2%, the only positive news was that the market is holding steady, anchored by U.S consumer sales numbers.[/align]
[font=Trebuchet MS][size=medium][i][size=x-small][url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-bonds/u-s-30-year-yields-drop-to-fresh-record-low-below-2-idUSKCN1V51PN]>>Source[/url][/size][/i]


[b][color=white]As Recession Concerns Mount, Dozens of Central Banks Are Cutting Rates[/color][/b][/size][/font]
[align=justify]Concerns about Brexit, trade wars and slowing global economic growth have driven banks to cut back on their interest rates to help stimulate borrowing and therefore prop up economies likely to be affected. Some of the surprises include New Zealand, India and Thailand, which lowered their interest rates. Even in the United States, Trump is urging the Federal Reserve to keep dropping its benchmark interest rates. All of this is being done to protect economies from the risk of a recession. Even if these interventions can help reduce the risks associated with a recession, they pose another problem: they could lead to a race to the bottom. In cutting interest rates and stimulating borrowing at home, governments weaken their currency to encourage the exportation of goods and services and discourage the importation of the same. The effect of this could be runaway currency depreciation around the world, unleashing the exact effects the interest rate cuts were supposed to prevent.[/align]
[font=Trebuchet MS][size=medium][i][size=x-small][url=https://www.nytimes.com/2019/08/15/business/economy/central-bank-rate-cuts.html]>>Source[/url][/size][/i]

[b][color=white]Alibaba earnings show Chinese consumers are still shopping despite trade war[/color][/b][/size][/font]
[align=justify]Even with the ongoing trade war between the United States and China, Chinese consumers are still spending. Alibaba reports that it saw a 40% growth in sales in its latest quarter. Even if growth was expected, the reported 40% was much better than had been predicted by analysts. Mobile users and improved sales in their Taobao and Tmall platforms are thought to be behind this growth. With this announcement, Alibaba shares rose about 3%. This rise was short-lived as the share price fell the following day amid fears of a U.S recession. Another core part of Alibaba’s business, Alibaba computing unit also saw a 66% growth in sales over last year’s sales.[/align]
[font=Trebuchet MS][size=medium][i][size=x-small][url=https://edition.cnn.com/2019/08/15/investing/alibaba-earnings/index.html]>>Source[/url][/size][/i]

[*][b][color=#66cc33]Gemini ♊[/color][/b]
